{{short description|Invariant measure that displays a less restricted form of ergodicity}}
In the mathematical discipline of [[ergodic theory]], a '''Sinai–Ruelle–Bowen (SRB) measure''' is an [[invariant measure]] that behaves similarly to, but is not an [[ergodic]] measure. In order to be ergodic, the time average would need to equal the space average for almost all initial states <math>x \in X</math>, with <math>X</math> being the [[phase space]].<ref name='walters'>{{cite book|last=Walters|first=Peter|title=An Introduction to Ergodic Theory|year=2000|publisher=Springer|isbn=0-387-95152-0}}</ref> For an SRB measure <math>\mu</math>, it suffices that the ergodicity condition be valid for initial states in a set <math>B(\mu)</math> of positive [[Lebesgue measure]].<ref name='bonatti-viana' />

The initial ideas pertaining to SRB measures were introduced by [[Yakov Sinai]], [[David Ruelle]] and [[Rufus Bowen]] in the less general area of [[Anosov diffeomorphism]]s and [[Axiom A|axiom A attractors]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Bowen | first1=Robert Edward|section=Ergodic theory of axiom A diffeomorphisms|title=Equilibrium States and the Ergodic Theory of Anosov Diffeomorphisms|series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics| date=2008|volume=470|pages=63–76|publisher=Springer|doi=10.1007/978-3-540-77695-6_4|doi-access=free| isbn=978-3-540-77605-5}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ruelle|first1=David|year=1976|title=A measure associated with axiom A attractors|journal=American Journal of Mathematics|volume=98|issue=3|pages=619–654|doi=10.2307/2373810|jstor=2373810}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Sinai|first1=Yakov G.|year=1972|title=Gibbs measures in ergodic theory|journal=Russian Mathematical Surveys|volume=27|issue=4|pages=21–69|doi=10.1070/RM1972v027n04ABEH001383}}</ref>

==Definition==

Let <math>T:X \rightarrow X</math> be a [[map (mathematics)|map]]. Then a measure <math>\mu</math> defined on <math>X</math> is an '''SRB measure''' if there exist <math>U \subset X</math> of positive Lebesgue measure, and <math>V \subset U</math> with same Lebesgue measure, such that:<ref name='bonatti-viana'>{{cite journal|author1=Bonatti, C.|author2=Viana, M.|year=2000|title=SRB measures for partially hyperbolic systems whose central direction is mostly contracting|journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]|volume=115|issue=1|pages=157–193|doi=10.1007/BF02810585|doi-access=free|s2cid=10139213}}</ref><ref name='metzger'>{{cite journal|author1=Metzger, R. J.|year=2000|title=Sinai–Ruelle–Bowen measures for contracting Lorenz maps and flows|journal=Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré C|volume=17|issue=2|pages=247–276|doi=10.1016/S0294-1449(00)00111-6|bibcode=2000AIHPC..17..247M|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/AIHPC_2000__17_2_247_0/|doi-access=free}}</ref>
:<math>
  \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i = 0}^n \varphi(T^i x) = \int_U \varphi \, d\mu
</math>
for every <math>x \in V</math> and every continuous function <math>\varphi: U \rightarrow \mathbb{R}</math>.

One can see the SRB measure <math>\mu</math> as one that satisfies the conclusions of [[ergodic theorems|Birkhoff's ergodic theorem]] on a smaller set contained in <math>X</math>.

==Existence of SRB measures==

The following theorem establishes sufficient conditions for the existence of SRB measures. It considers the case of Axiom A attractors, which is simpler, but it has been extended times to more general scenarios.<ref name='young'>{{cite journal|author1=Young, L. S.|year=2002|title=What are SRB measures, and which dynamical systems have them?|journal=Journal of Statistical Physics|volume=108|issue=5–6|pages=733–754|doi=10.1023/A:1019762724717|s2cid=14403405}}</ref>

'''Theorem 1:'''<ref name='young'/> Let <math>T: X \rightarrow X</math> be a <math>C^2</math> [[diffeomorphism]] with an [[Axiom A|Axiom A attractor]] <math>\mathcal{A} \subset X</math>. Assume that this attractor is ''irreducible'', that is, it is not the union of two other sets that are also invariant under <math>T</math>. Then there is a unique [[Borel algebra|Borelian]] measure <math>\mu</math>, with <math>\mu(X) = 1</math>,{{efn|If it does not integrate to one, there will be infinite such measures, each being equal to the other except for a multiplicative constant.}} characterized by the following equivalent statements:
# <math>\mu</math> is an SRB measure;
# <math>\mu</math> has absolutely continuous measures conditioned on the [[unstable manifold]] and submanifolds thereof;
# <math>h(T) = \int \log {\bigl| \det(D T)|_{E^u} \bigr|} \, d\mu</math>, where <math>h</math> is the [[Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy]], <math>E^u</math> is the unstable manifold and <math>D</math> is the [[differential operator]].
Also, in these conditions <math>\left(T, X, \mathcal{B}(X), \mu \right)</math> is a [[measure-preserving dynamical system]].

It has also been proved that the above are equivalent to stating that <math>\mu</math> equals the zero-noise limit [[stationary distribution]] of a [[Markov chain]] with states <math>T^i(x)</math>.<ref name='cowieson-young'>{{cite journal|author1=Cowieson, W.|author2=Young, L. S.|year=2005|title=SRB measures as zero-noise limits|journal=Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems|volume=25|issue=4|pages=1115–1138|doi=10.1017/S0143385704000604|s2cid=15640353}}</ref> That is, consider that to each point <math>x \in X</math> is associated a transition probability <math>P_\varepsilon(\cdot \mid x)</math> with noise level <math>\varepsilon</math> that measures the amount of uncertainty of the next state, in a way such that:
:<math>
  \lim_{\varepsilon \rightarrow 0} P_{\varepsilon}(\cdot \mid x) = \delta_{Tx}(\cdot),
</math>
where <math>\delta</math> is the [[Dirac measure]]. The zero-noise limit is the stationary distribution of this Markov chain when the noise level approaches zero. The importance of this is that it states mathematically that the SRB measure is a "good" approximation to practical cases where small amounts of noise exist,<ref name='cowieson-young'/> though nothing can be said about the amount of noise that is tolerable.
